I farm in Quzhou County, so I will stay with the pattern I trust most: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. That fits my age, my experience, and our local climate and water conditions. I do not want a fancy crop this year. I want a stable crop, familiar work rhythm, easier sales, and lower risk. I know how to manage wheat and maize, I can arrange fertilizer and irrigation by habit, and I can control labor better. For wheat, I will use improved seed, keep fertilizer moderate, irrigate a few key times, and aim for steady yield instead of chasing the highest yield. After wheat harvest, I will quickly sow summer maize with hybrid seed because maize responds well and gives reliable production here. I will keep tillage simple with rotary tillage, use enough nitrogen for maize, and control weeds and insects with a limited number of sprays. My main goal this year is steady output, manageable work, and not taking unnecessary risk.
